                    ### Question
                    Certain glucose transporters that are expressed predominantly on skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes are unique compared to those transporters found on other cell types within the body. Without directly affecting glucose transport in other cell types, which of the following would be most likely to selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Increased levels of circulating insulin
opb. Decreased levels of circulating insulin
opc. Increased plasma glucose concentration
opd. Decreased plasma glucose concentration
ope. It is physiologically impossible to selectively increase glucose uptake in specific cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Increased levels of circulating insulin would most likely selectively increase glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells and adipocytes. This is supported by the activation of insulin receptors on these cells, leading to increased translocation of glucose transporters (GLUT4) to the cell membrane, enhancing glucose uptake selectively in these cells.
